The '''2020–21 Danish Superliga''' (officially the '''3F Superliga''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 31st season of the [[Danish Superliga]].  The season began on 11 September with reigning champions [[FC Midtjylland]] playing against the winners of the [[2019–20 Danish Cup|Danish Cup]], [[SønderjyskE Fodbold|SønderjyskE]], losing 2–0 away from home. 

This season marked the first season with the [[video assistant referee]] (VAR) system.

==Teams==
Twelve teams competed in the league – the top ten teams from the previous season, the winner of the [[2019–20_Danish_Superliga#Relegation_play-offs|Relegation Playoffs]] and the champion of the [[2019–20 Danish 1st Division]]. [[Lyngby BK]] retained its position in the Superliga by winning the Relegation Playoffs and [[Vejle BK]] joined the top flight after winning the 1st Division title.

==European play-offs==
The fourth-placed team of the championship round, [[Aarhus Gymnastikforening|AGF]], advanced to a [[2021–22 UEFA Europa Conference League|Europa Conference League]] play-off match against the winning team of the relegation round, [[AaB Fodbold|AaB]]. The winners earned a place in the [[2021–22 UEFA Europa Conference League#Second qualifying round|Europa Conference League second qualifying round]].
